assumptions.choice: Treat the bar whose timestamp hour equals 15 (the 15:30 hourly bar, the final bar of each trading day in this feed) as both the 'last hour of the trading session' entry window and the 'end of the trading session' for the forced close rule.
assumptions.reason: The feed provides only 1h bars ending at 15:30; that single bar is the only one falling inside 15:00-16:00 and is also literally the last bar of the day, so it naturally serves both roles without inventing sub-hour data.

assumptions.choice: Take-profit and stop-loss are evaluated once per bar against the bar's Close price via market close orders in next(), not intrabar High/Low touches or broker stop/limit orders.
assumptions.reason: The spec states 'close the position when the price rises/falls by X%' without specifying stop-order mechanics or intrabar touch semantics, so a per-bar Close comparison is the most literal reading available with plain market orders.

assumptions.choice: Each entry size is 2% of current self.broker.getvalue() (mark-to-market equity at signal time) converted to whole shares via integer truncation.
assumptions.reason: The spec says '2% of total trading capital'; current portfolio value is the direct reading of that phrase, and integer share counts are the standard default for equity orders.

assumptions.choice: Daily volatility is computed as (day_high - day_low) / day_low, accumulated from the current day's bars up through the last-hour bar.
assumptions.reason: The spec does not state the denominator for expressing the high/low difference as a percentage; the day's low is the standard base for a range-percentage calculation.

assumptions.choice: 'RSI drops below 30 then rises above 30' (and the symmetric 70 case) is implemented as a same-bar crossover: rsi[-1] on the oversold/overbought side and rsi[0] back across the line, checked only on the last-hour bar.
assumptions.reason: Entries are only evaluated once per day, on the last-hour bar, so the crossover must be the transition observed at that exact bar; no separate multi-bar lookback window is specified.

assumptions.choice: No earnings-date or economic-news filter is implemented; the strategy trades on any day passing the volatility filter.
assumptions.reason: The environment supplies only OHLCV price data with no earnings calendar or news feed and permits only backtrader/math/collections/statistics imports, so this rule cannot be implemented without fabricating external data; the gap is declared rather than approximated.
